place: A small town of a few thousand people in Tamil Nadu, India
about: Every place-specific figure the town generator uses for a small Tamil Nadu town, with its source; where none was found or opened, the source says so (a PLACEHOLDER or 'to confirm'). Pay and pension are monthly in India and the structure counts fortnights. A world for another place and time is another profile; the platform's code holds none of these (docs/profiles.md).

unions.teaching: Together, workers win better pay and conditions than each alone.

kinds.name: temple, church and mosque congregation
kinds.teaching: There is a divine power that made the world and cares how we live.

attainment.label: Cannot read or has not finished primary school

sources.currency: Indian rupees, in paise: written with the rupee sign before the amount ("₹1,234.56"), or in words as rupees and paise (paisa singular, paise plural). ISO 4217: INR, two decimal places. Coinage Act 2011 (Government of India): the rupee is divided into 100 paise. The Indian grouping of digits (₹1,23,456, lakhs and crores) is not expressible: amounts are written in the western grouping.
sources.households: Household kinds are PLACEHOLDERS: the Census of India 2011 (household tables HH-01 and HH-11, Tamil Nadu: average household size 3.6) and NFHS-5 (Tamil Nadu, 2019-21) count households by size and head, but the household-type tables could not be opened here (to confirm: Registrar General and Census Commissioner, Census 2011, Houselisting tables, Tamil Nadu). Estimated shares: lone person 7%, couple alone 11%, couple with children 44%, one parent 9% (mostly widows), and 'group' 29% standing for extended and joint households (grandparents, in-laws, siblings' families), which the structure can only draw as 2-3 unrelated adults (a gap). children_couple and children_one_parent: placeholders shaped by Tamil Nadu's total fertility rate of 1.8 (NFHS-5, state fact sheet, 2019-21). same_sex_couple_bps: 0, because no count exists (the census does not record them); an absence of data, not a claim. lone_parent_female_bps 85%: placeholder (widowhood and desertion). adult_female_bps 50%: placeholder (Census 2011 sex ratio of Tamil Nadu, 996 females per 1,000 males; to confirm). child_male_bps: from NFHS-5 Tamil Nadu sex ratio at birth for births in the last five years, 878 females per 1,000 males (IIPS, NFHS-5 State Fact Sheet Compendium Phase II, Tamil Nadu, indicator 4: 1000/1878 = 53.2% male); a small-sample survey figure that is probably more skewed than the registered one (to confirm against SRS). mother_age_at_first_birth [20, 28]: placeholder around a median of about 23 (NFHS-5; to confirm). adult_ages, group_size, child_max_age: structure bounds, as in the other profile. Children at home are drawn to 24, a simplification: in India unmarried children stay home and many married sons stay with their parents.
sources.households.age_bands_bps: Registrar General of India, SRS Statistical Report 2020, Tamil Nadu (Statements 4-7): 0-4 years 5.6% of the population; under 15, 19.1%; 15-59, 69.2%; 60 and over, 11.7% (urban Tamil Nadu 12.8%). The 5-year splits inside those totals (5-9 and 10-14; each 5-year group within 15-59 and within 60+) are placeholders shaped by a typical age pyramid and scaled to the SRS totals. These are 2020 figures, not projected to 2026, when the older groups will be larger (National Commission on Population, Population Projections for India and States 2011-2036, gives Tamil Nadu 77.58 million in 2026; its age tables could not be opened, to confirm). 85 and over is taken to 99.
sources.fertility_per_10000: Registrar General of India, SRS Statistical Report 2020, Statement 21 (ASFRs, Tamil Nadu, 2020): births per 1,000 women of 5.6, 86.0, 123.7, 54.3, 15.0, 3.5 and 0.5 at 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44 and 45-49, times 10 (configs are integers). The total fertility rate these give is 1.4 (the report's figure for Tamil Nadu); NFHS-5 gives 1.8 for 2019-21.
sources.life.qx_per_100000: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, SRS Based Abridged Life Tables 2016-20, Tamil Nadu (total-population table, male and female nqx), read from the published PDF (censusindia.gov.in, catalog 44377, SRS-Abridged_Life_Tables_2016-2020.pdf): e.g. 0-1: 0.01942 male, 0.01785 female; 60-65: 0.08768, 0.06150; 80-85: 0.37019, 0.34437. Single-year probabilities per 100,000 are derived by spreading each interval's probability evenly in hazard (annual q = 1-(1-nqx)^(1/n)). Ages 85-100 are NOT published (the table ends at 85+): they extend the 80-84 hazard with a Gompertz slope of 9% a year, capped at 0.6 a year (a PLACEHOLDER). Life expectancy at birth in the table: 71.0 male, 75.5 female (73.2 total). The urban table is a little better (75.8 total); the state total is used.
sources.life.illness: PLACEHOLDER carried over from the other profile (no age-specific hospitalisation rates for Tamil Nadu were found). A source for India is NSS 75th round, Social Consumption: Health (2017-18), which gives hospitalisation rates by age and state (to source).
sources.life.injury: PLACEHOLDER carried over unchanged (no figure for Tamil Nadu was found); NSS 75th round (2017-18) gives hospitalisation by cause including injuries (to source). Severity split: placeholder.
sources.life.birth: Bearing a child from 15 to 49 (SRS age-specific fertility rates cover 15-49); 38 weeks from conception; female_bps 4675 from NFHS-5 Tamil Nadu: sex ratio at birth 878 females per 1,000 males for births in the last five years (IIPS, NFHS-5 State Fact Sheet Compendium Phase II, Tamil Nadu, indicator 4; 878/1878). A small-sample survey figure; to confirm against SRS.
sources.life.treatable: PLACEHOLDER carried over unchanged: the share of deaths that timely care could have prevented (treatable mortality, OECD and Eurostat definition: under 75 only). No Indian figure was found; India's share is likely higher (to source, e.g. Lancet Global Health Commission on High Quality Health Systems, 2018).
sources.life.found_alone_after: How long after dying at home alone a person is found. No figure for India was found. Japan's is used, as in the other profile, the one country found to count it: National Police Agency of Japan, people who died alone at home in 2025 (76,941), found within a day 28,398; 2-3 days 15,865; 4-7 days 10,456; 8 days or more 22,222 (read as reported in the press, to confirm). A PLACEHOLDER for a local figure: in India's joint households a person dying alone is rarer and probably found sooner.
sources.life.work_injury_bps: PLACEHOLDER carried over unchanged from the other profile (serious claims per million hours): no Indian figure was found. India's factory injury statistics (Directorate General Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes) and ESIC data exist (to source); injury in informal work is hardly recorded.
sources.ordinary_hours_per_week: Tamil Nadu Shops and Establishments Act 1947 and the Factories Act 1948 (s 51): at most 48 hours a week (to confirm the Tamil Nadu section; the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020, in force since 21 November 2025, keeps 48 hours; to confirm).
sources.wages_per_fortnight: Pay in India is monthly; the structure counts fortnights, so a monthly figure is x 12 / 26. Shop: Tamil Nadu Labour Department, minimum wage for Shops and Establishments from 1 April 2026 (notification Z3/3459/2026 of 18 February 2026), Zone D, support workers (peon, helper, shop assistant): basic plus variable dearness allowance, ₹13,823 a month, as summarised by a compliance site (dcpsol.com, 'Latest Minimum Wages for Shops and Establishments in Tamil Nadu'); the notification itself was not opened (to confirm). That is ₹6,379.85 a fortnight. Small shops often pay less (informal). Factory: PLACEHOLDER, about ₹15,000 a month for a regular manufacturing worker (the PLFS 2023-24 reports average earnings of regular wage or salaried workers by state and industry; not opened, to confirm). Construction: PLACEHOLDER, ₹650 a day x 13 working days a fortnight (casual labour in construction; Tamil Nadu Construction Workers Welfare Board and PLFS 2023-24 casual wage rates; not opened, to confirm).
sources.rents_per_month: PLACEHOLDERS, to source: monthly rents of ₹3,000, ₹4,500 and ₹6,000 for 1-3 bedroom flats and ₹6,500 and ₹8,500 for houses of 3 and 4 bedrooms in a small Tamil Nadu town, estimated at about one fortnight's shop wage for a 3-bedroom house (the ratio the other profile's rents have to wages). Sources to use: NSS 78th round, Multiple Indicator Survey (2020-21), rent paid by renter households; Census 2011, tenure and rent tables (Tamil Nadu); listings. The apartment mix and house shares are placeholders. Most rents in India are informal, set by agreement.
sources.spending.saving_bps: PLACEHOLDER, 8%: India's household sector saved about 18% of gross national disposable income in 2022-23, mostly in physical assets (housing, gold), and about 5% of GDP in financial assets (MoSPI, National Accounts Statistics; RBI, Handbook of Statistics on the Indian Economy; not opened, to confirm). A small-town household's saving out of income is taken as a figure in between.
sources.spending.wealth_effect_bps_per_year: PLACEHOLDER carried over unchanged from the other profile: about 3 paise of consumption a year per rupee of wealth (Dvornak & Kohler 2003, RBA RDP 2003-07, an Australian estimate; no Indian estimate found). A model's figure, not this place's.
sources.spending.essentials_per_month: PLACEHOLDER, ₹2,376 a person a month: the monthly per capita consumption expenditure of the poorest 5% of urban India (MoSPI, Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24 factsheet; recalled from the press note, not opened, to confirm). It stands for what a person spends however little comes in.
sources.spending.shops_known: How many sellers a household deals with and knows the prices of: 7 (Lengnick, M. (2013), 'Agent-based macroeconomics: A baseline model', Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization 86, Table 1: n = 7 type A connections). Not a figure of this place: a model's, kept until a survey of shoppers is found.
sources.spending.shop_search_bps_per_month: The monthly chance that a household looks at the price of a seller it does not deal with: 25% (Lengnick 2013, Table 1: 0.25 a month). A model's figure, not this place's.
sources.savings_by_age: PLACEHOLDER: an adult's cash and deposits (not gold, chit funds, provident fund, or property), by age: the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles. The other profile's placeholders scaled by half the ratio of the two shop wages (1.51), because Indian households hold less of their wealth in bank deposits (RBI, All India Debt and Investment Survey 2019 gives household assets by type; not opened, to confirm).
sources.retiree_savings: PLACEHOLDER: savings at retirement, about 2.25 to 5.25 lakh rupees, the other profile's placeholder scaled by 1.5. Most workers in India have no provident fund or pension (informal work); the EPFO and National Pension System are to be used to source this.
sources.retirement_age: 60: the age at which Tamil Nadu's government servants retire (Government of Tamil Nadu order of 2021 raising it from 59; to confirm) and at which the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension starts (National Social Assistance Programme guidelines). Self-employed and informal workers carry on working past it (gap).
sources.support.pension: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, Tamil Nadu: ₹1,200 a month for destitute persons (below the poverty line) aged 60 and over, made up of the Centre's ₹200 (60-79) or ₹500 (80 and over) and the State's top-up to ₹1,200 since August 2023 (Deccan Herald, 'Tamil Nadu enhances monthly pension for elders to Rs 1,200'; IMPRI, 'Tamil Nadu's Old Age Pension Scheme: Tracing Its Evolution Under the IGNOAPS Framework'; cra.tn.gov.in/about_schemes.php; as found by search, the pages not fully read, to confirm). It is means-tested to the poor; the structure pays every person from the age, so this overstates coverage (gap). Paid monthly, so every_days is 30.
sources.support.unemployment: None: India has no general unemployment benefit (the Employees' State Insurance scheme's Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana pays only some insured workers, and the rural employment guarantee gives up to 100 days of paid work a household, ₹319 a day in Tamil Nadu in 2024-25, which is work, not a transfer: Ministry of Rural Development, as reported; to confirm). The amount is 0, the closest the structure allows. Women heads of household in Tamil Nadu receive ₹1,000 a month (Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai, from September 2023; to confirm): not expressible (gap).
sources.firm_ownership: PLACEHOLDERS throughout, to source. Shops and landlords are held closely, as proprietorships and family firms: the National Sample Survey Office's survey of unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises (NSS 73rd round, 2015-16) found proprietary and partnership enterprises to be nearly all of them (to confirm). Factories in a small town are mostly family-owned small firms, with some branches of larger companies. Households holding shares directly: a small share of Indians hold equities (SEBI investor survey 2015: about 2% of households invest in the securities market; NSE Market Pulse; neither opened, to confirm); the shares by wealth fifth are guesses summing to a small total. The number of owners and owner wealth weights: guesses.
sources.retirement_fund: PLACEHOLDERS; used only by a world that asks for a retirement fund. The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and National Pension System stand for it. member_bps 12%: EPFO's active contributors are about 7 crore against a workforce of some 60 crore (EPFO annual report; PLFS; to confirm). cost_bps_of_income 0.5%: EPFO's administrative charge of 0.5% of wages (Employees' Provident Funds Scheme 1952, para 38; to confirm). share_bps_of_local: a guess. drawdown_bps_by_age: carried over from the other profile (account-based pensions are an Australian design); EPF pays most members a lump sum, not a pension (gap).
sources.industry: PLACEHOLDERS, to confirm: Annual Survey of Industries (MoSPI): manufacturing wages and total emoluments are about 10-11% of gross output and materials and fuels about 75% (recalled, not opened). Retail: purchases about 80% of sales and wages about 6% for small shops (placeholder; no source found).
sources.prices: PLACEHOLDERS: an item of goods worth ₹300 at world prices (the unit the town counts in), scaled from the other profile's unit by the ratio of the two shop wages (3.02); imports 10% dearer; inputs ₹7.50 a kg; building materials ₹3 a kg (cement about ₹7 a kg, bricks ₹2 to ₹3; Tamil Nadu retail prices not sourced).
sources.labour_force_participation_bps: PLACEHOLDER: the share of working-age adults (18 to 59) in the labour force, about 65%: PLFS 2023-24 (MoSPI) reports for Tamil Nadu a high male rate and a female rate under half (the state tables were not opened; to confirm). Those outside it (studying, caring) don't look for work.
sources.tenancy: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017: rent is revised by agreement, typically once a year (11-month agreements are customary), and a landlord gives three months' notice in writing of a revision (to confirm the sections, and whether the Act is in force as written). A tenant who stays on after the term holds over month to month (to confirm).
sources.values: PLACEHOLDER carried over unchanged: Schwartz's ten basic values, in the pan-cultural order found across 56 nations (Schwartz & Bardi 2001, 'Value hierarchies across cultures', Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology 32). Indian samples tend to rank tradition, conformity and security higher; not adjusted (to source, e.g. World Values Survey India wave).
sources.industrial_action: Industrial Relations Code 2020 (in force from 21 November 2025; to confirm), s 62: no worker in an industrial establishment may strike without notice within 60 days before striking, and not within 14 days of giving it (taken here as 14 days' notice). No strike ballot is required, so the turnout and approval thresholds are 0 (the structure has no 'no ballot' form). Employees on strike are not paid ('no work, no pay'; to confirm the section).
sources.world_price_process: PLACEHOLDER carried over unchanged: world prices move each month by a mean-reverting random process (sd of the monthly move in basis points; the share of a gap from the base kept each month). To estimate from India's Wholesale Price Index (Office of the Economic Adviser, by commodity).
sources.credit.cash_rate_bps: Reserve Bank of India policy repo rate, 5.25% (after the December 2025 cut). The October 2026 policy decision (5-7 October 2026) could not be confirmed: search results conflicted over whether it held at 5.25% or moved to 5.50% (to confirm).
sources.credit.funding_spread_bps: Placeholder: what a small bank pays over the policy rate for its funding.
sources.credit.lending_rate_bps: PLACEHOLDERS, to confirm: personal loans about 13% a year; loans to small businesses about 9% (RBI, weighted average lending rate on fresh rupee loans of scheduled commercial banks, Handbook of Statistics; not opened).
sources.credit.serviceability_buffer_bps: 0: India has no serviceability buffer rule like Australia's (the APRA buffer); the RBI leaves the affordability test to the lender (fixed-obligation-to-income ratio). The closest the structure allows is none.
sources.credit.max_repayment_share_bps: Placeholders: the most of a borrower's monthly income a lender lets repayments take (people 45%, the fixed-obligation-to-income ratio of 40-50% banks commonly apply to salaried personal loans, not sourced; organisations 20% of what comes in).
sources.credit.arrears_days: Placeholder: a month behind is arrears (a lender's first notice).
sources.credit.default_days: Non-performing at 90 days past due (RBI, Master Circular on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning; to confirm the current Master Direction).
sources.credit.max_months: Placeholder: the longest term for these loans (five years).
sources.credit.reserve: Placeholder: the cash the bank's lending office keeps back and doesn't lend, ₹302,000 (the other profile's placeholder scaled by the ratio of shop wages, 3.02). To source.
sources.opening: Placeholders, to source: what each organisation holds on the first day, scaled from the other profile's placeholders by the ratio of the two shop wages (3.02): the bank's own funds ₹1.51 million; the town ₹6.04 million; the builder ₹906,000; each landlord ₹1.81 million; a shop ₹90,600 where its working capital isn't worked out from its stock and wages; a factory ₹1.21 million; and the least an adult in the labour force has saved (₹3,000).
sources.town_finance: Placeholders, scaled from the other profile's by 3.02: the town's yearly parks line ₹453,000; the payment its procedure needs the mayor's written approval over, ₹151,000 (a town panchayat's financial delegation; Tamil Nadu Town Panchayats Act 1998; to source).
sources.public_finance.income_tax: Income-tax Act and Finance Act 2025, new tax regime (the default) for FY 2026-27 (as found on bankbazaar.com, 'Income Tax Slabs and Rates for FY 2026-27'; the Act not opened, to confirm): nil to ₹4 lakh; 5% to ₹8 lakh; 10% to ₹12 lakh; 15% to ₹16 lakh; 20% to ₹20 lakh; 25% to ₹24 lakh; 30% above. NOT EXPRESSED: the section 87A rebate (no tax at all up to ₹12 lakh of income), the standard deduction (₹75,000), and the 4% health and education cess on the tax (the structure's levy is a share of income, not of tax, so it is 0). In effect no one in a small town pays income tax, which is near the truth: only a small share of Indians do.
sources.public_finance.grants_per_resident_per_y: PLACEHOLDER, ₹1,500 a resident a year: Tamil Nadu's devolution to local bodies on the State Finance Commission's recommendation and Union grants under the Fifteenth Finance Commission (not opened, to source).
sources.public_finance.rates_per_resident_per_ye: PLACEHOLDER, ₹1,000 a resident a year of property tax and other own revenue; Indian municipalities' own revenue per head is small (RBI, Report on Municipal Finances; not opened, to confirm). Sets the town's opening rate in the rupee.
sources.public_finance.rates_instalments: Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act 1920 and Town Panchayats Act 1998: property tax is payable half-yearly (by 30 September and 31 March; to confirm the sections).
sources.public_finance.rates_due_days: Placeholder: an instalment falls due 30 days after its notice.
sources.public_finance.rates_penalty_interest_bp: Tamil Nadu local bodies charge 2% a month on unpaid property tax, 24% a year (not opened, to confirm).
sources.public_finance.rates_exempt_kinds: Government buildings, schools and charitable and public-health buildings are exempt from property tax under the municipal laws (to confirm the sections); the same kinds as the other profile are listed.
sources.public_finance.median_house_price: PLACEHOLDER, ₹20 lakh for a modest house in a small town: Tamil Nadu's guideline values (Registration Department) and listings are to be used (to source). The land value of a lot is derived from it less what the builder charges.
sources.services.waste_per_person_per_day_g: PLACEHOLDER, 400 g a person a day: urban India generates 0.3-0.5 kg a person a day (Central Pollution Control Board, Annual Report on Solid Waste Management 2020-21; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs; neither opened, to confirm Tamil Nadu's figure).
sources.services.landfill_levy_per_tonne: 0: no landfill levy was found in Tamil Nadu (the Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 provide for user fees and spot fines, not a levy per tonne; to confirm).
sources.services.council_staff_per_1000: PLACEHOLDER, 2 per 1,000: sanitary workers and council staff in a town panchayat (Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 and Tamil Nadu Municipal Administration Department staffing norms; not opened, to confirm). In the town, all of them are its works crew.
sources.services.collect_seconds_per_10kg: PLACEHOLDER carried over unchanged: about 12 seconds of work per 10 kg (a push-cart or tipper round in an Indian town is probably slower; to source).
sources.services.asset_life_years: PLACEHOLDER carried over: a park or civic building wears out in 15 years without upkeep.
sources.services.upkeep_hours_per_week_per_asset: PLACEHOLDER carried over: a crew member's half a day a week keeps a park or the hall up.
sources.services.complain_bps: PLACEHOLDER carried over: the chance a week that a household whose waste has gone two weeks uncollected writes to the town. A complaint rate is to be sourced (Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister's Helpline is the channel).
sources.unions.membership_bps: PLACEHOLDERS, to source: Labour Bureau, Trade Union Statistics (the last verified-membership report is for 2012-13); most workers are informal and unorganised (PLFS 2023-24 informal share; to confirm). Government employees' associations are the most organised, retail and construction the least. `other`, the overall rate.
sources.unions.dues_per_month: PLACEHOLDER, ₹30 a month: trade union dues in India are nominal (the Trade Unions Act 1926 sets a minimum subscription of 25 paise a month for registered unions; to confirm).
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Trade Unions Act 1926 (to confirm the section): a member may resign on notice in writing to the secretary, effective on receipt: 0 days.
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder carried over: a union claims the year's rise in prices and 2% more.
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: a members' meeting a month.
sources.unions.teaching: The union movement's claim, in words (content for belief). Its members hold it at the start.
sources.groups.kinds: PLACEHOLDERS: the kinds of social group (sport, religion, arts and culture, hobbies, community clubs); no Indian national survey of group membership was found. Women's self-help groups (Tamil Nadu Corporation for Development of Women, Mahalir Thittam) and temple committees are central in Tamil Nadu and have no kind of their own here (gap). How often each meets, and for how long: placeholders.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: one group of each kind for every 1,000 people.
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: PLACEHOLDER carried over (40%): the share of adults who belong to a group at the start and go to its gatherings. No Indian survey figure found (World Values Survey India wave, 'active membership', to source).
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: a member may leave a club or congregation at once.
sources.groups.kinds.teaching: What a group asks people to hold, in its words: content for belief to attach to. The congregation's stands for the town's faiths together (Hindu, Christian and Muslim; one congregation per town is a simplification), worded as belief in a divine power because they are not one doctrine.
sources.groups.kinds.held_at_start_bps: 97%: the share of Indians who believe in God (Pew Research Center, 'Religion in India: Tolerance and Segregation', 2021; to confirm). Census of India 2011, Tamil Nadu: Hindus 87.6%, Christians 6.1%, Muslims 5.9% (to confirm). At the start, the congregation's members hold its teaching strongly, and others up to this share hold it less.
sources.elections: Tamil Nadu Panchayats and Municipalities Acts: local bodies are elected for five years, by first-past-the-post in single-member wards; the town panchayat's chairperson is chosen by the councillors (Tamil Nadu State Election Commission, urban local body elections of 19 February 2022). This town elects its leader directly (a liberty). turnout: 74.68% in town panchayats at the 2022 urban local body elections (State Election Commission, as reported by The News Minute, 'TN urban polls: Overall voter turnout 60.7%'; the SEC's tables not opened, to confirm). Voting is not compulsory. stand_bps: placeholder, 2%. news_readers_bps: placeholder (Reuters Institute Digital News Report: India, to source).
sources.health: The clinic stands for the town's health system (a primary health centre or taluk hospital, and the private clinics and hospital it refers to; a liberty: a town of a few thousand has a primary health centre, not a hospital). doctors_per_1000: 130,898 registered allopathic doctors in Tamil Nadu (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, reply in Parliament, 2024, as found by search) at 80% availability (the Ministry's own assumption) over 77.58 million people (National Commission on Population, Population Projections for India and States 2011-2036, Tamil Nadu 2026): 1.35 per 1,000 (neither opened, to confirm). doctor_wage_per_fortnight: PLACEHOLDER, about ₹85,000 a month for an Assistant Surgeon in the Tamil Nadu Medical Services (pay matrix plus dearness allowance; to source). consult_minutes, seek_care_bps, treats and off_work_severities: placeholders carried over (the conditions here are hospital-level; in India much care is out of pocket at private providers and the poorest delay care: gap).
sources.education: school_ages: children start Class 1 at five or six and the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 makes school compulsory from 6 to 14; the town's school runs to Class 12, at 17 (Tamil Nadu School Education Department). students_per_teacher: 17 for Tamil Nadu in 2023-24 (UDISE+ 2023-24, Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education; primary 20, upper primary 18, secondary 11, higher secondary 33; as summarised by educationforallinindia.com, not opened, to confirm). school_days_per_year: 210 working days (Tamil Nadu School Education Department's academic calendar; to confirm). hours_per_day: about 6 (placeholder; Tamil Nadu schools run about 9:20 to 4:00). teacher_wage_per_fortnight: PLACEHOLDER, about ₹45,000 a month for a government school teacher (Tamil Nadu pay scales plus dearness allowance; to source). attainment: shaped by NFHS-5 Tamil Nadu: women literate 84.0%, men 90.7%; women with 10 or more years of schooling 56.6%, men 59.1% (IIPS, NFHS-5 State Fact Sheet, Tamil Nadu, indicators 14-17); the split between levels is a placeholder (to source from PLFS 2023-24, general educational level, Tamil Nadu), as years of schooling. return_per_year_bps: about 8% (Duraisamy 2002, 'Changes in returns to education in India, 1983-94', Economics of Education Review 21; estimates run 6-10%; to confirm), taken as productivity (Mincer 1974) and applied linearly in the time a task takes. max_years: the skill scale's top (placeholder).
sources.round: Working hours 9 to 5, six days a week (Tamil Nadu Shops and Establishments Act: 48 hours over six days; a liberty: the actual day is often 9 to 7 with a long break; not modelled); school 9 to 4 (placeholder; Tamil Nadu schools run about 9:20 to 4:00). Travel: off the roads, a 25 m cell on foot in about 18 seconds (walking about 1.4 m/s: Bohannon 1997); on a road, about 3 seconds (a two-wheeler or auto-rickshaw at about 30 km/h in a town; most small-town trips are by two-wheeler, bicycle or on foot; placeholder); slower across water, wetland and bush (placeholders). Roads: the town builds toward buildings more than three cells (75 m) from one (placeholder), within a roads budget scaled from the other profile's by the ratio of shop wages (3.02).
sources.ownership: house_owner_bps: PLACEHOLDER, 65%: Census 2011 (Houselisting tables, tenure status) gives roughly 70% owned in urban Tamil Nadu and more in rural (not opened, to confirm); flats here are all rented (a liberty). mortgage_bps_by_age: PLACEHOLDER; few Indian homeowners hold a mortgage (most build in stages from savings and family loans); NSS 78th round (2020-21) and RBI data on housing loans are to be used (to source). mortgage_payment_per_month: PLACEHOLDER, ₹8,000 (about a ₹9 lakh loan over 15 years at 8%). mortgage_rate_bps: PLACEHOLDER, 8.0%, the order of banks' home-loan rates after the 2025 repo cuts (to confirm). mortgage_years_left: placeholder. market: deposit_bps 10%: the RBI's loan-to-value ceiling is 90% for home loans up to ₹30 lakh (RBI Master Circular on Housing Finance, 2022; to confirm); costs_bps 9%: Tamil Nadu stamp duty of 7% and registration fee of 2% (Registration Department, Tamil Nadu; to confirm); mortgage_months 240: placeholder; buy_bps_per_month, relist_days, cut_bps and floor_bps: placeholders carried over (Merlo and Ortalo-Magne 2004).
sources.utilities: Water: PLACEHOLDER, 70 litres a person a day, the Tamil Nadu Water Supply and Drainage Board's supply norm for a town panchayat (TWAD Board design norms; recalled, not opened, to confirm); tariff PLACEHOLDERS ₹5 a kilolitre and ₹150 a quarter of service charges (many Tamil Nadu town panchayats charge a flat monthly fee; to source); bills go to owners. The river's inflow, flow and losses are placeholders carried over, sized so a small town's draw is a small share of a modest river's water. Energy (electricity): a Tamil Nadu household uses about 4 kWh a day (PLACEHOLDER; TNPDCL consumer data to source); the first 100 units each two months are free for all domestic consumers, 200 free for those under 500 units a billing period, then ₹4.70 a unit for 201-400 and ₹6.30 for 401-500 (Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission tariff order of 27 March 2025 and the Government's free-units scheme, as summarised by verified.realestate and the TNERC order, not fully opened, to confirm). The free block cannot be expressed: price_per_kwh is the 201-400 slab rate, so a typical household is charged for units it would get free (gap); supply_per_day 0 (no fixed charge for domestic tariff IA; to confirm). grid_price_per_kwh: PLACEHOLDER; TNPDCL's cost of supply is above its domestic tariff and the State pays the gap as a subsidy (₹173 billion to TNPDCL in 2026-27, powerline.net.in, 1 May 2026): not expressible, so the retailer's purchase price is placed below its sale price (gap). grid_emissions_g_per_kwh: 710 g, about India's grid average emission factor (Central Electricity Authority, CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, about 0.71-0.73 t/MWh; not opened, to confirm).
sources.climate: Weather drawn for each run (docs/behaviour/weather.md). rain_by_month_bps: Tamil Nadu gets about 52-55% of its rain in the Northeast Monsoon (October to December), about 30-32% in the Southwest Monsoon (June to September), November the wettest month (India Meteorological Department normals; Tamil Nadu agricultural university summaries for Thanjavur, as found by search; the monthly normals were not opened, to confirm). The month-by-month split (October 19%, November 21%, December 13%; June 5%, July 6%, August 9%, September 11%; January to May 16% together) is a PLACEHOLDER shaped on those shares; river flow is taken to follow rain. storm_*: PLACEHOLDERS: a heavy-rain spell (cyclone or depression, as in November 2015, December 2023, November 2024) in about one month in ten; the structure's storm chance is the same every month, but in Tamil Nadu it comes in October to December (a gap). drought_*: PLACEHOLDERS: about one year in ten starts a drought of six to eighteen months at 40% of usual inflow (the Northeast Monsoon failed badly in 2016-17; to source). Heatwaves: PLACEHOLDERS: summer is April to June, heat waves are rarer on the coast but hit the interior; three to five days, about one summer week in 17. Heat units and heat illness: carried over from the other profile (its source is Victorian, not Indian). warning_lead_days: IMD's early warnings a couple of days ahead (placeholder).
sources.hazards: Floods (world-expansion 7.3), PLACEHOLDERS carried over, sized against the river as modelled: it spills over its banks past 12,000 kL a cell, 30% of the excess a day; a building floods with water above 300 kL on its cell; wetland (tanks; Tamil Nadu has tens of thousands of irrigation tanks) soaks up 500 kL a cell a day. Tamil Nadu's recorded floods: Chennai 2015, Cauvery delta 2018 (Cyclone Gaja), Thoothukudi and Tirunelveli December 2023, Cyclone Fengal 2024 (Tamil Nadu State Disaster Management Authority; to source). Councils run relief centres: here the town hall.
sources.crime: Crime (world-expansion 7.2), deliberately rare and driven by circumstance only (need and opportunity, and the chance of being caught: Becker 1968; Cohen and Felson 1979), never by any group. take_bps_per_month_in_need, caught_bps_reckoned and take_quantity: placeholders. detection_bps: PLACEHOLDER carried over, 20% (National Crime Records Bureau, Crime in India, Tamil Nadu theft chargesheeting rate; not opened, to source). police_per_1000: PLACEHOLDER, 1.5: about 150 police per 100,000 people in Tamil Nadu (Bureau of Police Research and Development, Data on Police Organisations; not opened, to confirm). officer_wage_per_fortnight: PLACEHOLDER, about ₹30,000 a month for a Grade I police constable (Tamil Nadu Police pay matrix plus dearness allowance; to confirm). investigation_hours: placeholder.
sources.justice: The tribunal stands for the Rent Authority and the Labour Court (Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017; Industrial Relations Code 2020). hearing_after_days: PLACEHOLDER, four months to a first hearing (the National Judicial Data Grid shows long pendency in Indian subordinate courts; the figure is a guess, to source). pay_within_days: placeholder. challenge_bps and apply_bps: placeholders, lower than the other profile's, because few tenants or workers in the informal economy go to a court or the labour office (to source, e.g. Labour Bureau reports on disputes). apply_after_days: a month's wait for payment first (placeholder). Enforcement of an unpaid money order by attachment of the debtor's bank account (Code of Civil Procedure 1908, Order XXI; to confirm).
sources.nature: Nature (docs/design/world-expansion.md 2). cell_m: a cell is a 25 m lot. The landscape is a Cauvery-delta type: mostly paddy farmland (58%), tanks and wetland (7%), scrub (12%), grassland (15%) and little woodland (8%); Tamil Nadu's recorded forest and tree cover is about a fifth to a quarter of the state, mostly in the hills (India State of Forest Report 2023, Forest Survey of India; not opened, to confirm), so the plains share is lower. The shares, margin_cells, block_cells, woodland_patches, the covers' succession (cleared land to grassland in a year; scrub to woodland in about 30), the pollution figures, survey_hours_per_ha and survey_staff are PLACEHOLDERS. spin_up_years: nature is run alone this long before the start, so it begins in its own balance.
sources.nature.species: Real species of the region; every ecology figure (density_per_ha, home_range_ha, growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable, detection, barriers, tolerance) is a PLACEHOLDER from general natural history, to source from field studies. IUCN Red List status and protection: Indian star tortoise (Geochelone elegans), Vulnerable, dry scrub and grassland, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 Schedule IV, CITES Appendix I (listed here); Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), Least Concern, India's national bird, Schedule I; Indian pond heron (Ardeola grayii), Least Concern, wetlands, paddy and tanks; smooth-coated otter (Lutrogale perspicillata), Vulnerable, rivers and tanks, sensitive to pollution (listed here). The statuses are from memory of the IUCN Red List and not opened (to confirm).
